findings.title: GDN pair inversion preserves per-warp sequencing without extra group barriers
findings.before: Invert both chunks in place with group rendezvous between levels; two warps per chunk at widths 8/32/64, all four across each chunk's 16x16 diagonal blocks.
findings.after: Invert both A in place. Widths 8/32/64: warp[0:2] takes the first chunk and warp[2:4] the second. Width 16: warp r takes diagonal block r in the first chunk, then the second, without an intervening group join. Keep the level rendezvous.

metric.unit: normalized Unicode characters of value only

preservation.work: Both chunks, all prescribed diagonal blocks, one pair per chunk at widths 8/32/64; all four warps distribute the four blocks at width 16.
preservation.values: Existing inverse formulas and BF16 rounding retained.
preservation.storage: A remains in-place in Tring; Tinv publication remains after the inverse.
preservation.participants: warp[0:2] versus warp[2:4] on 8/32/64; warp r on block r in both chunks at width 16.
preservation.order_and_overlap: Each warp completes its chunk-0 block before its chunk-1 block; no additional all-four-warps barrier between those calls.
preservation.initialization_and_reuse: Original preparation, TMEM capture/return and Tinv/Beta reuse edges unchanged.

findings.deletion_counterexample: With member alone, all four warps can process whole chunks consecutively or duplicate blocks; same member range does not determine workload assignment.
findings.oversplitting_counterexample: Two whole-group serial width-16 chunk actions require done(chunk0 for all warps) before issue(chunk1), unlike source per-warp call order.
findings.expansion_cost: The previously shown width-8 extraction adds two static roles, two width-8 compute families and a join action, plus shared-warp entry/exit coordination. This is a concrete route cost, not a proven lower bound over all representations.

findings.title: FMHA advance can be shortened without deleting warp-collective participation
findings.before: Apply normalize and the numerator rescale using the retained Score and RowState. After the first group, any warp with an alpha unequal to one reads/multiplies/stores its NumState rows in 32-channel chunks and waits for the stores; all lanes of that warp participate. The first group never reads NumState. Compute probabilities and denominator partials, pack Prob8 into TMEM, then wait for its stores. A before-thread-sync fence and CTA barrier publish all probability and scale writes before thread 0's next PV. Score and group temporaries are now dead; MaxState, DenState, Prob8 and NumState retain their defined uses.
findings.after: Apply normalize to register Score from both compute:Score halves and carried RowState. After the first group, a warp rescales its TensorMemory.NumState rows iff any lane has alpha!=1; all its lanes participate. The first group never reads NumState. Complete NumState and TensorMemory.Prob8 writes, then join the CTA to publish Prob8 and preceding scale writes to the PV issuer. Retire Score and group temporaries; retain RowState, Prob8 and NumState.

findings.title: Local read retirement differs from output completion and from all-thread completion
findings.qsa_fact: After final Y-half read into registers, odrained is signaled before last output gate/store.
findings.fa4_fact: Each combine thread waits for its own copy and reads only its owned shared-memory slice; no per-stage CTA join exists.
findings.minimum_fa4_preservation_sentence: Each thread waits for and reads only its own copied slice; no per-stage CTA join.

preservation.work: FA4 four slots, initial three prefetches, per-thread last-valid-split clipping and nonpositive-weight skipping remain.
preservation.values: QSA retains the last register piece through gate/store; numerical formulas and rounding remain upstream.
preservation.storage: QSA two Y halves are distinct returned regions; FA4 copy/read partition is private.
preservation.participants: QSA requires both half-reader populations, not one warp or whole output completion; FA4 private readers remain local.
preservation.order_and_overlap: Next first PV may proceed after both Y-half releases while tail output work continues; FA4 does not acquire new per-stage CTA waits.
preservation.initialization_and_reuse: QSA final output sources no longer alias Y after capture; FA4 accumulators start from upstream zero and original prefetch/tail conditions remain.

findings.oversplitting_counterexample: Eight FA4 warp roles still cannot manufacture exact per-thread completion scope; a serial group stage done cannot be interpreted as private pointwise completion by name alone.
findings.minimal_representation_option: For private internal pipelines without external per-slice event consumers, retain them inside a higher-level action with explicit ownership and local order. Keep externally referenced boundaries in waiting.

findings.title: GDN final-mini conflict is a concrete missing source guarantee, not a missing schema field
findings.before:
Each warp follows its own instruction sequence without a CTA
join between readout, state update, output sweep and entry
into final-state staging. On the full path, form valid BF16
Out rows in RhsOutput from QS and Qd/Uh, compute the R update
using preloaded Kc fragments and DU, and rebuild Rh. Then
perform a warp join and sweep only that warp's staged Out
bytes into contiguous 16-byte stores to Out and optional core.
On the mini branch, Out was already written by rhs; read
row-0 Kc after the DU0 join, perform the rank-1 R update and
rebuild Rh, without the full-path readout or sweep.
Nonfinal chunks have no trailing CTA join: the next advance
retires the prior shared reads before stage/RhsOutput reuse.
On the last chunk, if FinalState is requested, each warp
immediately writes its R values to stage 0 at FP32 pitch
VTT+1, then joins the CTA to publish the staged final state.
Full-path overlapping K/Q/V reads were retired by earlier
joins/preloads. In a final mini chunk with (c_n-1)%NSTAGE=0,
stage-0 writes can race other warps' outstanding Kc row-0
reads; the source supplies no read-retirement guarantee.
Keeping this suffix in one action does not order those reads
before other warps' writes. Output global stores may still
be in flight; the source adds no separate store-drain wait.
findings.after: Each warp follows its own instruction sequence without a CTA join between readout, state update, output sweep and entry into final-state staging. On the full path, form valid BF16 Out rows in RhsOutput from QS and Qd/Uh, compute the R update using preloaded Kc fragments and DU, and rebuild Rh. Then perform a warp join and sweep only that warp's staged Out bytes into contiguous 16-byte stores to Out and optional core. On the mini branch, Out was already written by rhs; read row-0 Kc after the DU0 join, perform the rank-1 R update and rebuild Rh, without the full-path readout or sweep. Nonfinal chunks have no trailing CTA join: the next advance retires the prior shared reads before stage/RhsOutput reuse. On the last chunk, if FinalState is requested, each warp immediately writes its R values to stage 0 at FP32 pitch VTT+1, then joins the CTA to publish the staged final state. Full-path overlapping K/Q/V reads were retired by earlier joins/preloads. In a final mini chunk with (c_n-1)%NSTAGE=0, stage-0 writes can race other warps' outstanding Kc row-0 reads; the source supplies no read-retirement guarantee. Output global stores may still be in flight; the source adds no separate store-drain wait.

rejected_new_field.name: per-action member
reasons: A selector alone does not define per-warp independent issue order, condition scope or partial completion identities.
It does not solve FA4 per-thread private readiness.
The GDN ambiguity needs a short semantic clarification, and the QSA role expansion cost alone does not establish a net grammar benefit.

actual_read_scope.kind: targeted semantic audit; not a census of the ten operators
actual_read_scope.source_note: Read the source windows cited in findings plus surrounding control/setup ranges; did not read complete operator implementations or unrelated source variants.
actual_read_scope.scope_excluded: No evaluation of branch reuse, inheritance or root/dispatch organization; no cross-invocation study.

limitations: No GPU execution, race detector, full numerical equivalence proof or complete migrated Plan.
Fixed input YAML uses older vocabulary; snippets show current-field local directions, not a ready-to-submit whole document.
Character savings count only normalized scalar values. Full current noun registration and complete dependency migration may change total YAML length.
QSA static-warp decomposition is a source-backed direction and a scoped fragment, not a completed equivalence-checked rewrite.
Known missing source joins are retained as limitations; field additions cannot supply missing implementation guarantees.
